summary: Guthrie-Edmond Regional Airport (GOK) is a small general aviation facility serving Guthrie and the adjacent Edmond community in central Oklahoma, just north of the Oklahoma City metropolitan area. The airport primarily supports private pilots, flight training, and recreational flying, providing an alternative to the larger Will Rogers World Airport. Its location offers easy access to Guthrie's well-preserved historic downtown district, one of the largest on the National Register of Historic Places.
faqs:
Q: Does Guthrie-Edmond Regional Airport have commercial airline service?
A: No, GOK is a general aviation airport with no scheduled commercial flights. Travelers typically use Will Rogers World Airport in Oklahoma City for commercial service.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: The airport features runways, aircraft parking, fuel services, and basic amenities for private and general aviation operations.

Q: Can pilots rent aircraft or receive flight training at GOK?
A: As a general aviation airport in a growing metropolitan area, GOK supports flight training and private aviation activity, though specific rental and training availability should be confirmed directly with operators on field.

Q: Is the airport open to the public?
A: Yes, the airport is open to public use, though it primarily serves private pilots and aircraft owners rather than commercial passengers.
transport_tips: Since GOK has no commercial service, visitors typically arrive by personal vehicle, with the airport located just off US Route 77. Rental car services are not available on site, so arranging ground transportation in nearby Guthrie or Edmond is recommended. The drive to downtown Oklahoma City takes roughly 30 to 40 minutes depending on traffic.
local_tip: If you're flying into GOK, take advantage of Guthrie's walkable historic downtown, which features over 2,000 preserved Victorian-era buildings and hosts seasonal events like the Oklahoma International Bluegrass Festival.
